correctness.rationale: For total spin S, matched and universal inputs are S−s_v−s_w and S−s_u. At even order |S|≥2 gives consensus, including ties at |S|=2 by retention; at S=0 each homogeneous pair reverses, each mixed pair stays and each universal spin reverses. This preserves balance and is an involution, with fixed balanced states only for the perfect matching and all mixed pairs. At odd order |S|≥3 gives consensus. A step at |S|=1 homogenizes every pair and makes every universal spin agree with S. Thus any odd nonconsensus periodic state is on a critical level, with homogeneous pairs and all universal spins equal. For S=+1 and u positive universal spins, 4a−2m+2u−r=1 with a positive pairs, and the next total is 2u−1. With u=0 there is one +1 phase per orbit and the binomial index a=(n+1)/4 is feasible exactly under the stated congruence and inequality. With u=r≥3 the next total is noncritical. With u=r=1 and even m, both phases stay on one level, making half the central binomial count per level; the symmetric level restores the full count. This exhausts cycles and bounds entry by three steps (one for even n).
